subject: Invoice entity confirmation, MSA redlines & PO request
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@oakridge.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@oakridge.ai
Date: 2026-08-17T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Order form / invoice entity & tax certificate

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week — team is excited to move forward. Before procurement issues a PO we need a couple of clarifications on the Order Form:

- Can Redwood invoice the US entity (Oakridge AI, Inc.) for the Hosted API line items and the EU entity for any EU usage? We need explicit billing entity mapping on the Order Form appendix so finance can route invoices.
- What net terms do you expect? Our standard is Net 45 but we can do Net 30 on a pilot. Please confirm Redwood's preferred term.
- VAT vs withholding: we are VAT-registered in the UK/EU and will need a VAT invoice for EU billing. For US invoices, we will provide a W-9; if Redwood requires withholding for any reason, please confirm gross-up handling.
- Procurement asked for a stubbed Order Form we can review and a tax certificate (for our records).

I've attached our Tax Certificate for reference. Can you send back a version of the Order Form that clearly lists invoice entity, remit address, and payment terms? Also please confirm the DocuSign workflow so we can coordinate PO timing.

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Procurement
Oakridge AI

Attachments: Oakridge_Tax_Certificate.pdf
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@oakridge.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-17T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form / invoice entity & tax certificate

Hi Alice — great to hear and thanks for the clear ask. 

Short answers up front:
- We can map billing by entity in the Order Form appendix; draft attached (OrderForm_Appendix_v1.pdf). Please confirm which Oakridge legal entity to bill for production vs pilot usage.
- Standard Redwood hosted customers are invoiced Net 30 (our default), but our finance team can accept Net 45 on long-term commitments; I'll loop them in below so we can align.
- For EU VAT: we will provide VAT-compliant invoices when billing the EU entity; for US billing we'll request a W-9. If Oakridge requires withholding, our legal team typically asks for a gross-up clause (or alternate routing) — I'll include legal on thread.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm invoice entity and PO timing (we can provision on PO receipt).
2) Procurement reviews the attached appendix and returns any redlines.
3) If the appendix is accepted, we'll issue a DocuSign packet scoped to the entities you confirm.

I copied Ben (sales lead) to confirm commercial wrap and Kim (finance) for net terms / invoicing details. Karthik from legal will weigh in on any tax/gross-up language.

If you want, we can do a 15‑minute call tomorrow to walk the procurement team through the appendix.

Best,
Lauren Bishop

Hi all — looping in finance details. 

A few operational notes from payment ops:
- Redwood can accept Net 30 as our standard for hosted API customers. For customers requesting Net 45 we require a commercial sign-off and may need credit review. If Oakridge prefers Net 45, confirm whether that is for the entire term or only for the initial pilot.
- Please confirm billing entity full legal name, tax ID, billing address, and remit instructions. If US entity, provide W-9; if EU, provide VAT number.
- I've attached our Invoice Routing Template to make it quick for your procurement to return the PO with the correct mapping.

Once we have that, we can create invoice schedules and set the invoice delivery method (email vs AP portal). If Oakridge will split EU/US usage across entities, we need that mapping before the first invoice to avoid re-billing.

Kimberly Park
Director, Payment Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice@oakridge.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice entity confirmation, MSA redlines & PO request

Thanks — quick legal perspective and proposed redline items for the MSA / Order Form appendix. 

1) Tax allocation clause: we should add an explicit appendix row that maps each billed line item to the invoicing entity and the tax treatment ("VAT-treated / customer-registered" vs "US domestic taxable"). That reduces downstream disputes.

2) Withholding / gross-up: if Oakridge insists on withholding obligations on Redwood's payments, we should either: (a) require a gross-up equal to the withholding amount, or (b) route billing to a non-withheld entity if commercially acceptable. Please confirm Oakridge's stance.

3) W-9 / VAT evidence: include an evidence provision in the Order Form appendix allowing Redwood to rely on the supplied tax docs for invoice treatment; include a 30-day cure window for missing evidence.

4) Payment term flexibility: if finance approves Net 45, include a one-time 90 day credit review clause and an automatic reversion to Net 30 for renewals unless otherwise negotiated.

I can prepare a tracked-redline version of the MSA appendix but need confirmation on billing entities first (per Kimberly's ask). If procurement can confirm by EOD tomorrow, I'll turn around redlines within 48 hours.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

2) From Redwood: we've attached the OrderForm appendix (v1) and Payment Ops template; Kim has flagged Net 30 as default but can accept Net 45 pending credit.
3) Legal ask: if Oakridge will withhold taxes, please state that in reply — Karthik will add gross-up language or propose alternate routing.
4) DocuSign: once entity & PO confirmed, we'll send the Order Form packet via DocuSign (link below) targeted to the billing entity. Please confirm approver name(s) so signature routing is correct.
